origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

persons.note: A CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO PAPER OF 1833-1835 PRINTS THIS PERSON BY NAME IN THE TOWN. Read from newspaper_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 11 July 1835 and nothing says when they came. THE BOUND FALLS AFTER THE SCENE DATE and the record says so rather than narrowing it: the earliest source that names this person is later than 1 July 1835, so they may have arrived after the day this scene models. present_on_scene_date is `uncertain` for that reason. No figure is drawn (L1). THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 3 times, as “CLARK JOHN K”, 1834-11-04: 2 federal land entries — E2SE sec 06 T39N R14E; SW sec 11 T40N R13E, 240.00 acres stated in all, for $300.00 (ls0026, ls0027, ls0897). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS COOK, UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. The register states this purchaser's residence as COOK, so the sale is contemporary evidence that a man of this name lived in Cook County on the date of sale. It is not evidence that he lived in the town. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: CLARK JOHN K matches John K Clark: the forename names John K Clark of the 4 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

merge_ruling.for_merge: 'Chark' is one letter from Clark, h for l, and the forename 'John A.' agrees letter for letter with John K. Clark, in the American of 11 July 1835 (#c007). The stem 'Chark' is set nowhere in the deposited corpus and the town holds no other bearer of it: on the face of it a card minted off a garble.
merge_ruling.against_merge: A GARBLED READING CANNOT BE TESTED, AND THERE ARE TWO CLARKS IT COULD BE. R5 is the standing refusal and T-0695 is the ticket that reads these cards at the image; T-1027 files `chark_john_a` under the garbles in its own words — 'a fold here would repair a wreck by guessing at it'. The guess is not even single-valued: the town holds clark_john_a and clark_john_k, and the `clark-john` cluster has already ruled those two DISTINCT under D1 on their contradicting middle initials, so a fold of 'John A. Chark' would have to choose which of two ruled-apart men to join. Clark is set 2,655 times in the corpus and the reading index holds 37 Clark identities. R5, and the reading belongs to T-0695.

Both cards print an explicit middle initial and the two disagree — A against K — with no anchor on either side to say one of them is mis-set. Two men until something says otherwise, and the ruling is written onto both cards so the next pass does not re-ask.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 40 under 50', one of its male bands, conditioned on `named_on_a_roll_15_and_over` because the person is named in their own right on any other roll this layer was minted from - a letter list, a subscription, a court docket, a trade notice - or carries a role, a trade, a marriage or a parenthood.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('clark_john_k:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

sex_basis.note: A FORENAME THAT STANDS IN ONE SEX'S NAMING ONLY. 'John' is read as male because 14 persons in this layer whose sex a source records bear it (bates_john_jr, calhoun_john, caton_john_dean, davis_john, greene_john, hogan_john_s_c, and others), and it stands in the irish and yankee male forename pool of this town's own attested naming. Nothing about this person is recorded; the name is the whole of the reasoning, and the table that licenses it — data/research/residents/forename_sex.json — refuses a name its own evidence splits, refuses Jean, Marion, Leslie and Francis by name, and refuses an initial outright.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE CONSOLIDATED CIVIC, CHURCH, PRESS, BOOK AND CENSUS EVIDENCE (T-0513, T-0514). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.

arrival_year.note: A COMPILER'S TABLE, NOT A CONTEMPORARY RECORD, AND IT IS THE ONLY THING THAT PUTS THIS MAN AT CHICAGO BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago vol. 1 (1895), printed pages 78-79, the table headed LIST OF ACTUAL SETTLERS AT CHICAGO, PRIOR TO 1830, row bk_mose1_as_008: 'Clark, John K' — the scan closes the spaces to 'Clark.JohnK' — nativity ILLEGIBLE, YEAR 1817, remarks 'Paid taxes in 1825, voted in 1826'. The books crosswalk merges the row onto this card on the forename AND the middle initial, K being the rarest middle initial among the ten Clark cards this layer holds. WHY IT MATTERS HERE MORE THAN ON MOST CARDS: this household's `arrival` bound is 11 July 1835, which is AFTER the scene, so until this reading the layer held nothing that could see him at Chicago on 1 July 1835 at all. A man assessed in 1825 and polled in 1826 was living at the settlement. INFERRED AND NOT ATTESTED: the table is an 1895 compilation crediting Hurlbut's Chicago Antiquities pp. 37-8, every row transcription_mediated and none scan_verified; it dates a claim and does not prove it, which is the rung this project gives the Old Settlers roll for the same reason. THE NATIVITY IS A HOLE AND IS LEFT OPEN: the cell reads 'In-1' in the scan, with Ind. and Ire. both two characters away, and the reading records it as illegible rather than guessing — so `origin` is not edited by this and keeps its drawn region and its own replacement rule. WHAT DOES NOT FOLLOW: the table's preamble bounds it BEFORE 1830 and a man on it is not thereby at Chicago on 1835-07-01. `arrival`, `present_on_scene_date` and the grade are untouched; T-1144 owns the presence verdict and this reading is offered to it, not spent on its behalf.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. WHAT THIS PASS RULED ONTO THIS HOUSEHOLD, named so the ruling can be found again: each volume below is followed by the printed entries it set against this person and the status the crosswalk ruled them at — a single entry carries what its own `could_carry` declares, and an ambiguous or contested match carries nothing and is shown so that the silence is legible. clark_john_k, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 — f1839_e0286 (contested, so nothing crossed); clark_john_k, the advertising cards in Norris's directory of 1844 — n1844_ad0020 (contested, so nothing crossed).
